newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods- Buying, outage rejuvenate gasoline.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods- Buying, outage rejuvenate gasoline.

text.p: A Midwest refinery outage and solid refiner buying before the long Fourth of July weekend banished summer doldrums and gave differentials a firm boost in the Midwest and East Coast late Wednesday, players said.
Absolute prices were further bolstered by a 0.52 cent jump in August NYMEX gasoline, which settled at 59.29 cents a gallon.
But a morning Gulf Coast gasoline rally fizzled by late afternoon, with diffs actually ending a bit weaker than Thursday.
MIDCONTINENT

Unleaded gasoline differentials in the Chicago markets jumped more than one cent in late trade following news part of Citgo's 160,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) Lemont, Illinois, refinery will go down for planned maintenance on Monday.
The maintenance on an undisclosed portion of the plant will last until July 26, according to a source familiar with the company.
Citgo does not comment on refinery operations.

In moderate trade, differentials for prompt unleaded gasoline widened to between 1.75 cents and 2.0 cents over August NYMEX. Traders pegged any-months a quarter cent above Tuesday at 0.75/1.00 cents over the print.
Further bullish pressure came from rumors that an Ashland crude unit, which was shut by fire late Tuesday, will not return online for seven days instead of the previously reported one day.
The fire occurred at the 69,000 bpd St Paul Park, Minnesota, refinery, which was in the path of a severe electrical storm that hit the area.

Meanwhile, Group Three unleaded gasoline differentials firmed about a quarter cent with prompt barrels pegged at 2.25/2.50 cents over August NYMEX and any-month material unchanged at 0.75 cent over the print.
Players said bullish pressure from the refinery news was tempered somewhat by ample supply along the U.S. Gulf Coast-to-Midwest Explorer Pipeline. Supply was pegged at 20-days.
NEW YORK HARBOR
The East Coast market sprang to life Wednesday afternoon, with keen refiner interest in gasoline a marked contrast from near-standstill activity seen earlier in the week.

NYH conventional unleaded "M2" gasoline differentials firmed over a half cent a gallon by late day, with deals done at 2.50 cents under August futures as refiners stocked up for the three-day weekend, traders said.
"It was a pretty active day all the sudden. A lot of refiners were loading up -- Mobil, Amoco and Citgo," one player said, predicting the firmer values would hold until after the holiday.
Spot reformulated "A2" reformulated firmed only slightly, however, to about 0.10 cent below the August print, traders said.
On the distillate side, diffs held stable on heating oil, offered at 0.25 cent under the print, and on low sulfur diesel at 0.45 cent over the screen, players said.
U.S. GULF COAST
What went up at the Gulf Coast on Wednesday came down by late day, as "M1" southern grade regular conventional gasoline gave back all of its impressive early gains and more, traders said.

The bellwether gasoline grade ended the day at 1.75 cents under the August NYMEX gasoline print, but not before changing hands at levels as high as 1.00 cent under after starting the day out at around 1.50 cents.
"I don't think anyone wanted to come back on Monday (with unfinished business) with differentials moving the way they did," said one Gulf Coast trader.
Refiners and traders alike jumped in then out of the market, with differentials responding sensitively to their presence on the upside and to their absence on the downside.

The M1 may have gotten most of traders' attention on Wednesday, but decent volumes of distillate were changing hands as well, with distillate traders also interested in squaring their books before the end of the weekend.
But differentials were steady with Tuesday's levels.
Prompt back 19th cycle 74-grade low sulphur diesel traded at 1.80 cents under August NYMEX, and slightly deferred front 20th cycle was done at a 1.70 cents discount to August NYMEX.
Also, prompt 86-grade heating oil traded at 2.45, 2.40 and 2.35 cents under August futures.

Also, prompt cycle airline-quality 54-grade jet fuel was rumored to have been done at 0.05, 0.15 and 0.25 cent over the August print, while prompt low sulphur 55-grade jet fuel was heard done at 0.40 cent over August futures.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
